architecture.editorial_thesis: In 2026-W39 the frontier got cheaper and more operational: OpenAI pushed GPT-6 Sol/Luna to half price with a caching stack for persistent agents while Anthropic answered with Opus 5.5 at Fable-level performance for 40% less; Cursor industrialized the agent lifecycle with measured harness efficiency and post-PR bots; local inference, agentic science, evaluation, and privacy architecture each moved on first-party authority; vendor numbers stay attributed and late-only signals stay late.
architecture_goals: Present GPT-6 Sol/Luna as a cost-efficiency release with price card, availability, and attributed benchmarks plus the caching stack, not as a capability break with Astra
Present Opus 5.5 as a cost-performance challenger with pricing, safeguards, and X demo signal, keeping vendor-run figures attributed
Present Cursor harness efficiency and Rollouts/Security Review as measured agent operations with production-method bounds
Present Grok 4.7 as a coding-model release with quarantined effort-asymmetric claims and no invented community momentum
Present HF GGUF support as a scoped local-inference integration with explicit hardware and arch limits
Present ART enzyme discovery, MentalHealthBench, and DolphinBench as science and evaluation advances with pre-review and grader boundaries
Present Google server-side memory as a forward-looking privacy architecture with no availability claim
